criteria.text: Output distinguishes configured, auto-detected, and defaulted for every emitted key
A strict mode exits non-zero and names every key that resolved only to a default
Default non-strict output remains backward compatible for existing readers
Skills that require a project-specific binding to be real — integration branch, verify commands — treat a defaulted value as blocked and report it, rather than proceeding on the default
Covered by the binding-resolution test suite, including the no-config and not-a-repository cases
Every living skill and workflow consumer resolves project policy once through `resolve-project` and uses the returned `ResolvedProject` without a second policy read.
No living source or installed-skill reference invokes `resolve-bindings`; historical point-in-time artifacts remain unchanged.
Legacy default-fallback behavior is deleted or quarantined so it cannot serve a living consumer.
Managed source and installed skill trees pass the same zero-reference and behavior checks.
Fixtures for missing configuration, malformed configuration, a non-repository directory, and generated-projection drift fail closed with the resolver's documented error shape.
